articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg. Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai. Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14. Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month. The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot. Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month. The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot. articles.title: Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts. Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15. “Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). “He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others. “He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said. The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands. “The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary. “The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal. “His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 01:14:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts. Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15. “Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). “He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others. “He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said. The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands. “The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary. “The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal. “His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts. Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15. “Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS). “He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others. “He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said. The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands. “The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary. “The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal. “His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

articles.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable rockets

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality. The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems, a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream. “I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.” It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive, resource-intensive venture. The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Mr. Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex, because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters. “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!” Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Analyst Kathleen Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 06:25:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable rockets

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality. The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems, a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream. “I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.” It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive, resource-intensive venture. The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Mr. Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex, because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters. “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!” Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Analyst Kathleen Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Feasibility (Noun)
व्यवहार्यता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Feasibility' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Achievement (Adjective)
उपलब्धि — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Achievement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable..." (Hinglish Arth: स्टारशिप कक्षा से लौटी और टेक्सास में स्पेसएक्स के स्टारबेस लॉन्च पैड पर "चॉपस्टिक आर्म्स" द्वारा पकड़ी गई, जो पूरी तरह से पुन: प्रयोज्य रॉकेटों के लिए एक मील का पत्थर है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा, "स्पेसएक्स को संवेदनशील पेलोड और मिशनों को संभालने के लिए क्षमता को साबित करने के लिए कई बार की सफलताओं की आवश्यकता है।")

articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering. More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016. Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year. By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire. New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system. Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities. Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: One-third of deaths occur at home or elsewhere in the community, where burials and other procedures are often conducted without specialist supervision, increasing the risk of transmission.

1. Core Context & Background: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016

Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year. By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire. New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system. Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities. articles.title: What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure . This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions . Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness. As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community. Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs. Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household. Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health. Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .” But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”

Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .” But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”

hinglishTracks.en: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — पुरानी बीमारी वाले रोगियों के लिए स्वस्थ भोजन तक पहुंच को दवाओं के समान ही आवश्यक माना जाएगा।

hinglishTracks.en: Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — ढेर सारे वैज्ञानिक प्रमाण हमारे स्वास्थ्य पर खाने की आदतों के नकारात्मक और सकारात्मक दोनों प्रभावों का समर्थन करते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Scientific' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: वैज्ञानिक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Scientific' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — शोध से पता चलता है कि स्वस्थ आहार टाइप 2 मधुमेह, हृदय रोग और उच्च रक्तचाप जैसी पुरानी स्वास्थ्य स्थितियों से पीड़ित लोगों की मदद कर सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: This is where “food is medicine” comes in.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — यहीं पर "भोजन औषधि है" की बात आती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — भोजन औषधि है, जिसे "भोजन को औषधि के रूप में" और "खाद्य नुस्खे" के रूप में भी जाना जाता है, एक आंदोलन है जो विशिष्ट नैदानिक ​​​​स्थितियों को रोकने, प्रबंधित करने या इलाज करने के लिए चिकित्सक के नुस्खे के आधार पर स्वस्थ भोजन - फल, सब्जियां और कभी-कभी स्वस्थ प्रोटीन प्रदान करने के लिए समर्पित है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Prescription' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: नुस्खा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prescription' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — रोगियों को भोजन निर्धारित करने का उद्देश्य यह बताना है कि स्वास्थ्य और कल्याण के लिए भोजन उतना ही महत्वपूर्ण है जितना कि दवा।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Prescription' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: नुस्खा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prescription' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — शोधकर्ताओं के रूप में जिनका काम ग्रामीण समुदायों में भोजन की पहुंच और स्वास्थ्य पर केंद्रित है, हमारे पास उत्तरी मिसिसिपी में हमारे स्थानीय क्षेत्र में खाद्य चिकित्सा कार्यक्रम चलाने का प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — भोजन ही औषधि है कार्यक्रम क्यूरेटेड फूड बॉक्स, किराना वाउचर और चिकित्सकीय रूप से तैयार भोजन के माध्यम से वितरित किया जा सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 01:05:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure . This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions . Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness. As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community. Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs. Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household. Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health. Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .” But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found. Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age. Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said. "Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy. Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes. "While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said. "Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 12:39:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found. Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age. Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said. "Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy. Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes. "While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said. "Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure. These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others. The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 11:52:52 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure. These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others. The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

Organisation (Noun)
संगठन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Organisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Association (Noun)
संगठन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Association' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. (Hinglish Arth: इसके लिए उद्योगों, बिजली संयंत्रों, आवासीय खाना पकाने और अन्य दहन गतिविधियों सहित प्रमुख स्रोतों पर उत्सर्जन में कटौती की आवश्यकता है।")

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution. Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas. Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said. In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)." Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16. Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function. Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies. The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change. However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support. According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health. The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days. Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems. “We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said. He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves. “At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 11:45:28 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies. The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change. However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support. According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health. The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days. Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems. “We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said. He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves. “At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

Congenital (Adjective)
जन्मजात — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Congenital' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Conference (Noun)
सम्मेलन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conference' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregna' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pre' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pre' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns." (Hinglish Arth: अध्ययनों से पता चलता है कि अत्यधिक गर्मी के संपर्क में आने से गर्भवती महिलाओं के स्वास्थ्य, गर्भावस्था के परिणाम और नवजात शिशुओं के स्वास्थ्य पर असर पड़ सकता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. “That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The episode discusses the everyday realities of living with diabetes, experiences of older adults who have managed the condition over several years, and practical approaches to diabetes management, including diet, physical activity and blood glucose monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 59th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, marking World Diabetes Day, explores the everyday realities of living with diabetes and approaches to managing the condition over time. Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to individuals living with diabetes, including older adults who share their experiences of managing the condition over several years. Their experiences offer perspectives on living with diabetes and the importance of sustained management. The episode also features a discussion with Dr. V. Mohan, Chairman and Chief of Diabetology, Dr. Mohan’s Diabetes Specialities Centre, Chennai, on practical approaches to diabetes care. The discussion looks at the role of dietary habits and food choices in diabetes management, the importance of regular physical activity and exercise, and blood glucose monitoring. It also examines how sustainable changes to everyday food and activity routines can support long-term management of the condition. The episode discusses practical measures that people living with diabetes can incorporate into their daily lives, the importance of consistent approaches to care, and how genetic predisposition and environmental factors influence the development and management of diabetes. It also explores longevity and living well with diabetes over the years.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Health Wrap Episode 59 discusses living with diabetes, approaches to diabetes care and more

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 11:35:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The episode discusses the everyday realities of living with diabetes, experiences of older adults who have managed the condition over several years, and practical approaches to diabetes management, including diet, physical activity and blood glucose monitoring

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 59th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, marking World Diabetes Day, explores the everyday realities of living with diabetes and approaches to managing the condition over time. Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to individuals living with diabetes, including older adults who share their experiences of managing the condition over several years. Their experiences offer perspectives on living with diabetes and the importance of sustained management. The episode also features a discussion with Dr. V. Mohan, Chairman and Chief of Diabetology, Dr. Mohan’s Diabetes Specialities Centre, Chennai, on practical approaches to diabetes care. The discussion looks at the role of dietary habits and food choices in diabetes management, the importance of regular physical activity and exercise, and blood glucose monitoring. It also examines how sustainable changes to everyday food and activity routines can support long-term management of the condition. The episode discusses practical measures that people living with diabetes can incorporate into their daily lives, the importance of consistent approaches to care, and how genetic predisposition and environmental factors influence the development and management of diabetes. It also explores longevity and living well with diabetes over the years.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: Assam Congress writes to PM, seeks enhanced aid for victims of Kaziranga accident
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In the letter, Debabrata Saikia expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Assam Congress leader Debabrata Saikia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to enhance compensation for victims of the Kaziranga minibus-truck collision , provide free treatment to the injured and livelihood assistance to families of the 26 deceased. In the letter, the former leader of the opposition in the Assembly expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing. Mr. Saikia demanded a thorough examination of the road's condition, design, maintenance, traffic management and safety arrangements, as well as urgent intervention on highway safety, healthcare and infrastructure of the region. Appreciating the Prime Minister for announcing financial assistance immediately after the accident, he added that the magnitude of the tragedy demanded enhanced compensation and rehabilitation measures. Administrative accountability must be fixed while the conduct of the drivers involved must also be investigated, the Congress leader said in the letter while expressing disappointment over the response of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who visited the accident site a day later on Saturday (November 14, 2026). Mr. Saikia claimed that while Mr. Sarma announced ex gratia and promised a probe into the accident, his remarks had failed to adequately address the grievances of locals about the highway. He also referred to the Chief Minister's reported remarks about a possible medical emergency involving the deceased driver, saying this should not divert attention from potential deficiencies in highway infrastructure. At least 26 people died, including minors, and 20 others were injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), officials said. Many of the victims were college students. The Congress leader further said that Mr. Sarma himself had acknowledged that certain traffic restrictions had previously been relaxed under political pressure, making an independent examination of administrative decisions necessary. In the letter, he also raised concerns relating to the Kaziranga region, including the NH-715 safety, healthcare facilities, alleged misuse of hospital premises, environmental protection, expansion of the eco-sensitive zone and land acquisitions, among others.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Saikia sought an increase in total compensation to the next of kin of each deceased to at least ₹20 lakh, inclusive of the ₹9 lakh already announced by the Central and State Governments, with additional assistance for families losing multiple members.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Assam Congress writes to PM, seeks enhanced aid for victims of Kaziranga accident

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 03:19:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In the letter, Debabrata Saikia expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Assam Congress leader Debabrata Saikia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to enhance compensation for victims of the Kaziranga minibus-truck collision , provide free treatment to the injured and livelihood assistance to families of the 26 deceased. In the letter, the former leader of the opposition in the Assembly expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing. Mr. Saikia demanded a thorough examination of the road's condition, design, maintenance, traffic management and safety arrangements, as well as urgent intervention on highway safety, healthcare and infrastructure of the region. Appreciating the Prime Minister for announcing financial assistance immediately after the accident, he added that the magnitude of the tragedy demanded enhanced compensation and rehabilitation measures. Administrative accountability must be fixed while the conduct of the drivers involved must also be investigated, the Congress leader said in the letter while expressing disappointment over the response of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who visited the accident site a day later on Saturday (November 14, 2026). Mr. Saikia claimed that while Mr. Sarma announced ex gratia and promised a probe into the accident, his remarks had failed to adequately address the grievances of locals about the highway. He also referred to the Chief Minister's reported remarks about a possible medical emergency involving the deceased driver, saying this should not divert attention from potential deficiencies in highway infrastructure. At least 26 people died, including minors, and 20 others were injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), officials said. Many of the victims were college students. The Congress leader further said that Mr. Sarma himself had acknowledged that certain traffic restrictions had previously been relaxed under political pressure, making an independent examination of administrative decisions necessary. In the letter, he also raised concerns relating to the Kaziranga region, including the NH-715 safety, healthcare facilities, alleged misuse of hospital premises, environmental protection, expansion of the eco-sensitive zone and land acquisitions, among others.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Saikia sought an increase in total compensation to the next of kin of each deceased to at least ₹20 lakh, inclusive of the ₹9 lakh already announced by the Central and State Governments, with additional assistance for families losing multiple members.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Inclusive (Adjective)
समावेशी — जिसमें समाज के हर वर्ग (खासकर गरीब और वंचित वर्ग) को बराबर शामिल किया जाए।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Egalitarian, All-encompassing  |  ✖ Ant: Exclusive, Discriminatory, Narrow
Rehabilitation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Rehabilitation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Mizoram village revels in return of World War II-hit festival
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Serkawn hosts the three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival, initiating a series of winter tourism events planned to crescendo with Christmas and New Year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A village in south-central Mizoram’s Lunglei district has revelled in the return of a festival that was an indirect casualty of the Second World War 80 years ago. Serkawn, about 175 km south of Aizawl, the State’s capital, organised the Serkawn Contest from 1932 to 1946 to celebrate the musical heritage and emerging creative talent in the erstwhile Lushai Hills. It was not held in 1942 due to World War 2, but the toll the conflict took on the global economy killed the concert after four years. The concert staged a comeback at Serkawn from November 11 to 13 in a new avatar—the Leitlangpui Music Festival. It marked the return of a “heritage event” to a location deeply rooted in the history of modern Mizo music. The Union Ministry of Tourism and the Mizoram Tourism Department organised the event with Bbyanimals as the official event partner. “Music is an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity, and Serkawn holds a special place in the story of our musical journey. Bringing the Leitlangpui Music Festival back to Serkawn is not simply about hosting an event at a historic location; it is about reconnecting generations with a legacy, celebrating the talent of our people and creating new possibilities for the future,” Mizoram’s Tourism Minsiter, Lalnghinghlova Hmar, said. “Our vision is to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to a wider national and international audience, while ensuring that such platforms create meaningful opportunities for our young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities,” he said. The performers at the Serkawn festival included Deborah Ralte, C.T. Tluangtea, Benjamin Sum, Fenga, Sangtei Khuptong, David Darlong, Lil Kiki, Evenflow, Swordtune, Avora Records, Knot, RNZX, Dingtea Guite, Saka, Serkawn Band, Rokhumbeu, Johan, Your Sweetest Memories, Ruatpuii and Triautrackx. Beyond its musical programme, the festival brought together a range of commercial and entrepreneurial activities, including food and beverage businesses, local vendors, commercial exhibitors, traditional handicrafts, handloom products, fashion and lifestyle offerings. Mizoram recorded 7.37 lakh tourists from January to September 2026, which was 2.236 lakh more than the corresponding period in 2025. The total domestic and foreign tourist count in 2025 was 8.41 lakh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to the sharp increase in tourist footfall, Mr. Hmar highlighted the role of festivals and cultural events in attracting visitors, creating livelihood opportunities and strengthening local economies.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (15 NOV)

📰 Mizoram village revels in return of World War II-hit festival

📌 Published: 15 Nov 2026, 03:17:33 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Serkawn hosts the three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival, initiating a series of winter tourism events planned to crescendo with Christmas and New Year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A village in south-central Mizoram’s Lunglei district has revelled in the return of a festival that was an indirect casualty of the Second World War 80 years ago. Serkawn, about 175 km south of Aizawl, the State’s capital, organised the Serkawn Contest from 1932 to 1946 to celebrate the musical heritage and emerging creative talent in the erstwhile Lushai Hills. It was not held in 1942 due to World War 2, but the toll the conflict took on the global economy killed the concert after four years. The concert staged a comeback at Serkawn from November 11 to 13 in a new avatar—the Leitlangpui Music Festival. It marked the return of a “heritage event” to a location deeply rooted in the history of modern Mizo music. The Union Ministry of Tourism and the Mizoram Tourism Department organised the event with Bbyanimals as the official event partner. “Music is an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity, and Serkawn holds a special place in the story of our musical journey. Bringing the Leitlangpui Music Festival back to Serkawn is not simply about hosting an event at a historic location; it is about reconnecting generations with a legacy, celebrating the talent of our people and creating new possibilities for the future,” Mizoram’s Tourism Minsiter, Lalnghinghlova Hmar, said. “Our vision is to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to a wider national and international audience, while ensuring that such platforms create meaningful opportunities for our young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities,” he said. The performers at the Serkawn festival included Deborah Ralte, C.T. Tluangtea, Benjamin Sum, Fenga, Sangtei Khuptong, David Darlong, Lil Kiki, Evenflow, Swordtune, Avora Records, Knot, RNZX, Dingtea Guite, Saka, Serkawn Band, Rokhumbeu, Johan, Your Sweetest Memories, Ruatpuii and Triautrackx. Beyond its musical programme, the festival brought together a range of commercial and entrepreneurial activities, including food and beverage businesses, local vendors, commercial exhibitors, traditional handicrafts, handloom products, fashion and lifestyle offerings. Mizoram recorded 7.37 lakh tourists from January to September 2026, which was 2.236 lakh more than the corresponding period in 2025. The total domestic and foreign tourist count in 2025 was 8.41 lakh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Referring to the sharp increase in tourist footfall, Mr. Hmar highlighted the role of festivals and cultural events in attracting visitors, creating livelihood opportunities and strengthening local economies.
